text:
sam (oncall): heads up — we’re seeing a spike in etcd commit latency in eu-west-2; apiserver 502s across a few zones and controller-manager restarted a couple times. GPU onboarding jobs are stuck Pending. anyone looking? :thinking:

marta: saw the same. etcd leader moved twice in ~3m and disk iops for the leader node is pegged. apiserver logs show heavy timeouts on watch requests.

raj: NAT gateway errors in eu-west-2 earlier — egress failures to our storage backend. could be snapshot uploads blocking WAL flushes?

josh: pasting quick outputs i grabbed:
```
# kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o wide
etcd-eu-west2-0   1/1     Running   0     28m   10.3.5.12   eu-west-2a
etcd-eu-west2-1   0/1     CrashLoop  5     24m   10.3.6.14   eu-west-2b
```

lin: controller-manager logs show repeated "failed to create watch: i/o timeout" and then OOMKill. watch queue backlog looks huge.

sam (oncall): ok mitigation plan suggestions? can we throttle controllers or demote apiserver traffic to a fallback region?

marta: short term — reduce controller concurrency for heavy controllers (replicasets, jobs) and pause large batch onboarding. I can push a canary config to lower --concurrent-gc-syncs and controller flags.

raj: also open ticket with cloud infra — request temporary extra burst iops for the affected disk, and check NAT health. if egress to storage is failing WAL replication will stall.

josh: doing controller flag change now:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy controller-manager --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=2","--concurrent-job-syncs=1"]}]}}}}'
```

infra-bot: alert: etcd_commit_latency > 200ms (eu-west-2) — incident ticket #INC-2027 created.

lin: i scaled down a bunch of noncritical workloads in eu-west-2 dev namespace to free nodes for GPU onboarding. GPU pod Pending reason still shows "Insufficient resources: ports, nvidia.com/gpu" — likely scheduler decision due to taints and capacity.

marta: added a temporary node pool with relaxed taints in eu-west-2c (spot GPUs) to clear the provisioning backlog; rolling up now.

sam (oncall): good. monitor etcd leader — if the leader OOMs again we should failover reads to follower replicas and schedule leader relocation during low traffic. also we should tighten watch timeouts to avoid apiserver thrashing.

raj: cloud replied — NAT had a short throttling window, they increased SNAT table and applied a patch. they also granted a temporary iops bump on the etcd leader disk (5x) for 60m.

josh: after controller flag patch and node pool, GPU queue drained ~40% in 12m. apiserver 5xxs dropped to baseline. watch latency still elevated but trending down.

sam (oncall): rolling postmortem tasks: (1) evaluate WAL upload backpressure and snapshot scheduling, (2) add runbook step to scale controller concurrency, (3) investigate NAT saturation alerts -> permanent SNAT capacity increase for eu-west-2, (4) consider read-only apiserver endpoints in other regions for heavy watch consumers.

marta: noted — I’ll open the RFC for the permanent SNAT / IOPS budget change.

lin: leaving a note: if anyone runs cluster-e2e load tests, tag eu-west-2 so we don’t trigger this during peak.

sam (oncall): thanks team. keeping incident open for now until metrics stable for 30m. :thumbsup:
